meaning_reference_en: as for; marks the topic of the sentence
notes_reference_en: Written は but pronounced 'wa'. It sets up what the sentence is about; the key information comes after it.

meaning_reference_en: marks the subject; points out new or focused information
notes_reference_en: Question words such as だれ and 何 take が, never は, when they are the subject. が is also used with 好き, ほしい, 上手 and わかる for the thing liked, wanted or understood.

meaning_reference_en: marks the direct object of a verb; marks a place moved through or left
notes_reference_en: Written を but pronounced 'o'. With movement verbs such as 歩く, 散歩する and 出る it marks the route or the place being left.

meaning_reference_en: at; on; in (a specific point in time)
notes_reference_en: Used with clock times, dates, days of the week and months. Relative words such as 今日, 明日, 毎日 and 来週 take no に.

formation_reference_en: Noun + に + 行く / 来る / 帰る
notes_reference_en: Close in meaning to へ. に puts the focus on the arrival point, へ on the direction.

formation_reference_en: Noun + に + ある / いる
meaning_reference_en: in; at; on (where someone or something is)
notes_reference_en: Used with ある, いる and 住む. For the place where an action happens (eat, study, play), use で instead.

meaning_reference_en: to (the person who receives or is the target of an action)
notes_reference_en: Common with あげる, 貸す, 教える, 見せる, 電話をかける and 会う. With もらう and 借りる, に marks the person you get something from.

meaning_reference_en: per; in (how many times within a period)
notes_reference_en: The period comes first, then に, then the number of times: 月に一回 (once a month).
Written へ but pronounced 'e'. Usually interchangeable with に for destinations; へ stresses the direction a little more.

meaning_reference_en: at; in (the place where an action happens)
notes_reference_en: Compare 教室にいます (being somewhere: に) with 教室で勉強します (doing something there: で).

meaning_reference_en: by; with; in (means, tool, method or language)
notes_reference_en: To say 'on foot', use 歩いて行きます rather than で.

meaning_reference_en: and (joining nouns in a complete list)
notes_reference_en: と lists every item; to give just some examples, use や. It joins nouns only, not verbs or adjectives.

meaning_reference_en: with; together with (a partner in an action)
notes_reference_en: Often followed by いっしょに. With verbs like 話す, 会う and 結婚する, と marks the other person.

meaning_reference_en: and (giving some examples out of more); ... and so on
notes_reference_en: Suggests the list is not complete. Often ends with など: 本や雑誌など.
Means one of the items is chosen. To list items together, use と or や.

meaning_reference_en: also; too; (with a negative) not ... either; neither ... nor
notes_reference_en: も replaces は, が and を, but comes after other particles: 京都にも行きました.
The first noun describes the second: 日本の車 (a Japanese car). The second noun can be dropped when clear: それは私のです.

meaning_reference_en: from (a starting point in time or place)
notes_reference_en: Often paired with まで: 月曜日から金曜日まで (from Monday to Friday).

meaning_reference_en: until; up to; as far as
notes_reference_en: Marks the end point of something that continues. For a deadline ('by'), use までに (N4).

meaning_reference_en: (question marker) turns a sentence into a question
notes_reference_en: Polite questions end in か and are usually written with 。. In casual speech か is normally dropped and rising intonation is used instead.

meaning_reference_en: isn't it?; right? (seeking agreement or sharing a feeling)
notes_reference_en: Used when the speaker expects the listener to share the same view or knowledge. Compare よ, which tells the listener something new.

meaning_reference_en: you know; I tell you (giving new information or emphasis)
notes_reference_en: Tells the listener something they may not know. Overusing it with superiors can sound pushy.
In X は Y より + adjective, Y is the standard. Japanese adjectives have no '-er' form; より does that job.

formation_reference_en: Noun + の方が + Noun + より
notes_reference_en: The two parts can come in either order. Often used to answer a どちら question.

formation_reference_en: Noun + と + Noun + とどちらが
meaning_reference_en: which is more ..., X or Y?
notes_reference_en: Compares exactly two things. どっち is the casual form of どちら. Answer with 〜の方が.

formation_reference_en: Noun + の中で + Noun + が一番
notes_reference_en: Used for three or more items. In questions use 何, だれ, どこ or いつ before が一番.

formation_reference_en: Noun + です / na-Adj + です / i-Adj + です
notes_reference_en: Forms: です, ではありません, でした, ではありませんでした. After an い-adjective, です only adds politeness: 高いです.
Forms: だ, じゃない, だった, じゃなかった. Never used right after an い-adjective (高いだ is wrong). Often dropped in casual questions: 学生？

formation_reference_en: Noun + ではありません / na-Adj + ではありません / Noun + じゃない / na-Adj + じゃない
meaning_reference_en: is not; am not; are not
notes_reference_en: じゃありません and じゃないです are more conversational polite forms. Past: ではありませんでした / じゃなかった. い-adjectives use 〜くない instead.

formation_reference_en: Noun + でした / na-Adj + でした
notes_reference_en: Past negative: ではありませんでした. い-adjectives do not take でした: say 高かったです, not 高いでした.

meaning_reference_en: polite non-past verb ending (do; will do)
notes_reference_en: Covers habits and future actions. 飲む→飲みます, 食べる→食べます, する→します, 来る→来ます.
The plain equivalent is the ない-form: 飲みません = 飲まない.
The plain equivalent is the た-form: 会いました = 会った.
The plain equivalent is 〜なかった: 食べませんでした = 食べなかった.

meaning_reference_en: do not; will not (plain negative of verbs)
notes_reference_en: う-verbs change the last -u sound to -a: 書く→書かない, 買う→買わない. る-verbs drop る: 食べない. する→しない, 来る→こない, ある→ない. Past: 〜なかった.
Made exactly like the て-form, with て→た and で→だ: 書いて→書いた, 飲んで→飲んだ, 行って→行った. Polite equivalent: 〜ました.
Used when the speaker expects the listener to agree. To invite more gently, use 〜ませんか.
Offers to do something for the listener (shall I?) or asks them to decide something together (shall we?).

meaning_reference_en: won't you ...?; would you like to ...? (polite invitation)
notes_reference_en: Gentler than 〜ましょう because it leaves the listener room to decline. Accept with ええ、〜ましょう.
Conjugates like an い-adjective: 〜たくない, 〜たかった. The object can take が or を. Not used to state another person's wishes directly.
For things, not actions (actions use 〜たい). Conjugates like an い-adjective: ほしくない, ほしかった.
Used when shopping or ordering. A quantity goes after を with no particle: 切手を二枚ください.
Polite, but still an instruction the speaker expects to be followed. Softer requests use 〜てくれませんか (N4).
Softer than 〜てはいけません. In casual speech ください is dropped: 見ないで.
Add ですか to ask for permission. A polite refusal is often just すみません、ちょっと….
A strong prohibition, often for rules. Polite form: 〜てはいけません. Casual contraction: 〜ちゃいけない / 〜じゃいけない.

pattern: 〜なければならない / 〜なくてはいけない
formation_reference_en: Verb-nai stem + なければならない / Verb-nai stem + なくてはいけない
notes_reference_en: Polite forms end in なりません / いけません. The two mean the same; なければならない sounds slightly more formal.

formation_reference_en: Verb-nai stem + なくてもいい
notes_reference_en: The opposite of 〜なければならない. Ask with 〜なくてもいいですか (Is it all right if I don't ...?).

meaning_reference_en: be doing (ongoing action); be in a state (result of a change); do regularly
notes_reference_en: With action verbs (食べる, 読む) it shows an action in progress; with change verbs (結婚する, 開く, 知る) it shows the resulting state. Polite: 〜ています.

meaning_reference_en: and; and then (linking actions in order)
notes_reference_en: The final verb sets the tense for the whole sentence. 書く→書いて, 飲む→飲んで, 話す→話して, 買う→買って, 行く→行って (irregular).

meaning_reference_en: after doing; (do A) and then (B); since
notes_reference_en: Stresses that A is finished before B starts, more clearly than a plain て. With ている in the main clause it often means 'since'.

formation_reference_en: Verb-ta + り + Verb-ta + りする
meaning_reference_en: do things like A and B; sometimes A, sometimes B
notes_reference_en: Picks out a few actions from many. Tense and politeness go on the final する: 〜たりしました.

meaning_reference_en: have (ever) done; have the experience of doing
notes_reference_en: Talks about life experience, not something just done: きのう食べたことがある is wrong. Negative 〜たことがありません means 'have never'.

formation_reference_en: Verb-dict + 前に / Noun + の + 前に
notes_reference_en: The verb before 前に is always in dictionary form, even when talking about the past. With a length of time there is no の: 3年前に (three years ago).

formation_reference_en: Verb-ta + 後で / Noun + の + 後で
notes_reference_en: The verb before 後で is always in た-form, even for future plans. On its own, 後で means 'later'.

meaning_reference_en: while (doing two actions at the same time)
notes_reference_en: Both actions are done by the same person. The main action comes last: in A-ながら B, B is the main activity.

formation_reference_en: Verb-stem + に行く / Noun + に行く
notes_reference_en: 来る and 帰る work the same way: 遊びに来る. With する-nouns the noun can come directly: 買い物に行く, 散歩に行く.

formation_reference_en: Noun + が好き / Noun + が嫌い / Verb-dict + の + が好き
notes_reference_en: 好き and 嫌い are な-adjectives, so the thing liked takes が, not を. 大好き and 大嫌い are stronger. 嫌い can sound blunt; あまり好きじゃない is softer.

formation_reference_en: Noun + が上手 / Noun + が下手
notes_reference_en: Mostly used about other people; calling yourself 上手 can sound like bragging. Both are な-adjectives: 料理が上手な人.

formation_reference_en: Noun + がある / Noun + がいる
meaning_reference_en: there is; there are; have (ある for things, いる for people and animals)
notes_reference_en: ある is for things, plants and events; いる is for people and animals. Negatives: ない / いない (polite: ありません / いません).
The reason comes first: A から B (A, so B). Answer どうして with 〜からです. Nouns and な-adjectives need だ: 雨だから.
Also used just to soften a request or lead into a topic: すみませんが…. A little more formal than けど (N4).

formation_reference_en: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + でしょう
notes_reference_en: Typical of weather forecasts. Said with rising intonation, it asks the listener to agree. Plain form: だろう (N4).

formation_reference_en: i-Adj-ku + なる / na-Adj + になる / Noun + になる
notes_reference_en: いい becomes よくなる. Often used in the past to describe a change that has happened: 大きくなりました.
Common when ordering food or picking from options. Past: 〜にしました (I decided on ...).

formation_reference_en: まだ + Verb-te + いない / まだ + Verb-te + いません
notes_reference_en: Use ていない, not ませんでした, for something that may still happen. The short answer is いいえ、まだです.

formation_reference_en: もう + Verb-ta / もう + Verb-stem + ました
notes_reference_en: In questions もう means 'yet'. With a negative verb, もう means 'no longer': もう食べません.

formation_reference_en: あまり + Verb-nai / あまり + i-Adj-ku + ない / あまり + na-Adj + じゃない
meaning_reference_en: not very; not much; not often
notes_reference_en: Always followed by a negative form. あまり好きじゃない is a softer way to say you dislike something.

formation_reference_en: 全然 + Verb-nai / 全然 + i-Adj-ku + ない / 全然 + na-Adj + じゃない
meaning_reference_en: not at all; not in the least
notes_reference_en: Stronger than あまり〜ない. In casual speech 全然 is sometimes used with positive words (全然大丈夫), but with a negative is the standard use.

formation_reference_en: Noun + だけ / Verb-dict + だけ
notes_reference_en: Neutral in tone. Compare しか〜ない (N4), which stresses that the amount is small.

formation_reference_en: Noun + くらい / Noun + ぐらい
meaning_reference_en: about; approximately (an amount or length of time)
notes_reference_en: Used with amounts and durations. For a point in time (around three o'clock), use ごろ: 3時ごろ.
Attaches to clock times, dates and months. に after ごろ is optional: 7時ごろ(に)起きます.

pattern: 何も〜ない / 誰も〜ない
reading: なにも〜ない / だれも〜ない
romaji: nani mo ... nai / dare mo ... nai
formation_reference_en: 何も + Verb-nai / 誰も + Verb-nai
meaning_reference_en: nothing; nobody; not anything; not anyone
notes_reference_en: With places, a particle comes before も: どこにも / どこへも行きません (go nowhere). 誰 is often written in hiragana: だれ.

pattern: 何か / 誰か / どこか
reading: なにか / だれか / どこか
romaji: nani ka / dare ka / doko ka
notes_reference_en: Question word + か gives 'some-' words; question word + も + negative gives 'no-' words. が and を after 何か / だれか are often dropped.

pattern: これ / それ / あれ / どれ
formation_reference_en: これ / それ / あれ / どれ
meaning_reference_en: this one; that one (near you); that one (over there); which one
notes_reference_en: こ = near the speaker, そ = near the listener, あ = away from both, ど = question. They stand alone; as a subject どれ takes が, not は.

pattern: この / その / あの / どの
formation_reference_en: この / その / あの / どの + Noun
meaning_reference_en: this; that (near you); that ... over there; which (before a noun)
notes_reference_en: Always followed by a noun: この本, never この alone. これ / それ / あれ / どれ are used when there is no noun.

pattern: ここ / そこ / あそこ / どこ
formation_reference_en: ここ / そこ / あそこ / どこ
meaning_reference_en: here; there (near you); over there; where
notes_reference_en: こちら / そちら / あちら / どちら are politer versions: お国はどちらですか (Where are you from?).

formation_reference_en: i-Adj stem + くない / i-Adj stem + かった / i-Adj stem + くなかった
meaning_reference_en: negative and past forms of i-adjectives (is not; was; was not)
notes_reference_en: 高い→高くない, 高かった, 高くなかった. Add です to be polite. いい is irregular: よくない, よかった, よくなかった.

formation_reference_en: na-Adj + な + Noun / na-Adj + です / na-Adj + ではありません / na-Adj + でした
meaning_reference_en: na-adjectives: take な before a noun and です or だ at the end of a sentence
notes_reference_en: Before a noun, add な: 静かな部屋. At the end of a sentence they change like nouns. きれい and きらい end in い but are な-adjectives.

formation_reference_en: i-Adj-ku + て / na-Adj + で / Noun + で
notes_reference_en: いい becomes よくて. Join qualities that point the same way (both good or both bad); for a contrast, use が instead.
Introduces a name the listener may not know.
